Privileges Committee

The responsibility of this committee is: to review and study matters submitted to the committee concerning the privileges of the Majlis and its members and the conduct of members of the Majlis; to check whether anything has occurred that infringes the privileges of members, and, if an infringement has occurred, to establish and state how and why it happened and set out the action to be taken; to determine measures that may be taken to prevent such a thing from happening in future and [?] further measures to be taken and further principles; when a member is accused of having done something in violation of the law and the rules, to look into and investigate the matter and advise the Speaker of the Majlis on the action to be taken; to give [?] advice to members, officers or staff on monitoring their conduct in line with the standards of conduct; to set the principles for accepting and giving gifts; to set and enforce the principles and standards for disclosure of members' financial [?]; and to prepare reports on these matters and submit them to the Majlis.

3. How the committee carried out its work

Article 259 of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis states that if the Speaker or the Secretary General of the People's Majlis receives information, as provided in Article 258 of the Rules, that a member of the People's Majlis has been detained, this committee must be informed immediately, within 24 (twenty-four) hours, and that once so informed, this committee must meet at the earliest possible opportunity to look into the matter. Accordingly, when this committee received information that Kendhoo constituency MP Mauroof Zakir of the People's Majlis had been taken into police custody during a protest being held by fishermen on 11 December 2025, the committee held its 13th meeting of 2025 on 11 December 2025 and discussed the matter. The committee also decided that the Secretariat [?] send a letter to the Maldives Police Service to [?] ensure that the member is afforded the human rights and privileges he is entitled to [?] while Kendhoo constituency MP Mauroof Zakir of the People's Majlis was in police custody, and to clarify [?] the member [?] in police custody [?].

In addition, the committee received letters sent by some members of the People's Majlis seeking the member's statement, and a document sent by Kendhoo constituency MP Mauroof Zakir [?] his complaint. Further, in connection with the matters noted and the questions raised in those documents, the committee decided at its 03rd meeting of 2026, held on 6 May 2026, to obtain from the Maldives Police Service the facts of how events unfolded in the matter. Accordingly, once the Maldives Police Service had shared that information with the committee, the committee began its review of the matter.

4. Matters noted by the committee

4.1. That the Maldives Police Service informed the committee on 12 December 2025, by its letter number 171-G(MCI)/57/2025/119, that Kendhoo constituency MP Mauroof Zakir of the People's Majlis was arrested for showing conduct such as disobeying the orders of the security forces while taking part in the protest being held by fishermen at sea opposite Jetty No. 1 from 10 December 2025 onwards, and

That the Maldives Police Service informed the committee on 07 October 2026, by its letter number 171-PHQ/57/2026/31, that when Kendhoo constituency MP Mauroof Zakir was examined at 20:00 on 11 December 2025, no [?] from the arrest was noted; however, as the member requested to see a doctor, he was seen by a doctor at Dhoonidhoo clinic at 20:50 that day; that when the member was again seen by a doctor at Dhoonidhoo clinic at 08:43 on 13 December 2025, [?] for further treatment he was taken to IGMH that day and seen by a [?] specialist; and that, as the medical condition then [?] keep in detention [?], the member was released from police custody.

5. The committee's decision

In the matter of Kendhoo constituency MP Mauroof Zakir of the People's Majlis being taken into police custody during a protest being held by fishermen on 11 December 2025, after discussion at the committee's 07th meeting of 2026, held on 19 October 2026, the committee decided, by consensus of the members who took part in the decision, that the privileges of Kendhoo constituency MP Mauroof Zakir of the People's Majlis were not infringed when he was taken into police custody, [?] of the way the Maldives Police Service acted in arresting the member, and [?] to the committee.

[signature]

Therefore, in accordance with Article 260(a) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, we submit the report on the committee's review of this matter to the Speaker of the People's Majlis.

The letter sent to the committee by the Secretary General of the People's Majlis, as the Maldives Police Service had shared information that Kendhoo constituency MP Mauroof Zakir of the People's Majlis was taken into police custody during a protest being held by fishermen on 11 December 2025, is attached as "Schedule-1".

Further, details of members' attendance at the committee meetings held to review the matter of Kendhoo constituency MP Mauroof Zakir of the People's Majlis being taken into police custody during a protest being held by fishermen on 11 December 2025 are included as "Schedule-2" of this report.
